input.reason: The request is purely a display-order change on the watchlist page. The watchlist component owns the rendered list through its `movies` signal, so sorting there (unwatched first, stable within groups) satisfies the request without altering the store's data/persistence contract or any other consumer.

steps.instruction: The watchlist page must show movies the user has not watched yet before movies already watched. Concretely: the `movies` signal must return the list ordered so that every item with `watched === false` comes before every item with `watched === true`. Within each group, preserve the current relative order of the underlying store items (stable sort over `store.items()`, e.g. `[...items].sort((a, b) => Number(a.watched) - Number(b.watched))` — Array#sort is stable). The ordering must be reactive: when `toggleWatched` changes an item's watched status, the item must immediately move to the other group (a newly watched movie appears after all unwatched movies; unwatching it moves it back among the unwatched ones, per stable order). The template must render the list from this sorted `movies` signal so the visible order is unwatched first, watched last. Do not change the WatchlistStore unit or its stored/insertion order, and do not change any exported signatures — `movies` stays `Signal<WatchItem[]>`. If an existing test of yours pins the old insertion-order display, submit a change request for it instead of editing it.

Clicking a row's checkbox, and clicking the blank space of a row, must still call store.toggleWatched with the id of the movie rendered in that row, flipping that movie's watched flag. You must NOT make a watched movie appear before an unwatched one to satisfy the failing tests. Do not change exported signatures, do not touch watchlist-store or its stored/insertion order, and do not modify or remove any existing test (use the change-request protocol instead). content.text:
## Diagnosis

The wiring is intact — cause **2** applies:

- The template binds `(change)="toggleWatched(movie.id)"` on each checkbox and `(click)="onRowClick($event, movie.id)"` on each row, with the id taken from the same `@for (movie of movies(); track movie.id)` loop iteration. Clicking row 0's checkbox / blank space calls `store.toggleWatched(1)` and flips Movie 1 — evidenced by the checkbox test's *later* assertions (`watchedCount() === 1`, subtitle `'1 of 2 watched'`) which pass with my implementation.
- Both tests fail at `expect(checkbox().checked).toBe(true)` because `checkbox()` **re-queries the first rendered row after the click**. Under the required order, the just-watched Movie 1 moves behind the still-unwatched Movie 2, so `items()[0]` is now Movie 2, whose checkbox is unchecked → "expected false to be true". The assertions pin the old order (toggled movie stays at index 0), which this request supersedes.

Per the instruction I keep my implementation unchanged (the three acceptance failures are your setup issue; my template's `RouterLink` stays), leave both failing tests untouched, and file a change request for each. I added two new tests that document the required order and pass with the current code.

testChangeReasons.reason: Cause 2 — the assertions encode the OLD display order, the click wiring is intact. Clicking the first row's checkbox still fires (change)="toggleWatched(movie.id)" with Movie 1's id and store.toggleWatched(1) flips Movie 1 to watched; this test's later assertions (watchedCount() === 1 and subtitle '1 of 2 watched') already pass with my implementation. It fails on the first assertion, expect(checkbox().checked).toBe(true), because checkbox() re-queries the FIRST rendered row after the toggle. Under the required order (every unwatched movie before every watched one, stable within groups), the just-watched Movie 1 moves behind the still-unwatched Movie 2, so the first rendered row is now Movie 2 with an unchecked checkbox — hence 'expected false to be true'. The assertion pins the superseded old order (the toggled movie staying at index 0); the only way to satisfy it as written would be to render a watched movie before an unwatched one, which the hard constraints forbid. Request: keep the toggle intent but assert the new position, e.g. checkbox(1).checked === true (the watched movie now renders last) and/or store.items()[0].watched === true.
testChangeReasons.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when the checkbox is clicked

testChangeReasons.reason: Cause 2 — same diagnosis. items()[0].click() on the blank space of the first row (Movie 1) reaches onRowClick (the li is not inside an a/button/input, so the guard passes) and correctly calls store.toggleWatched(1); Movie 1 does become watched. The failure is at expect(checkbox().checked).toBe(true): checkbox() re-queries the first rendered row after the reactive re-sort, and the now-watched Movie 1 renders behind the still-unwatched Movie 2, so the first row's checkbox is Movie 2's unchecked one — 'expected false to be true'. The assertion pins the old order (toggled movie stays at the top), which this request supersedes. Request: keep the row-click toggle intent but assert the toggled movie at its new position, e.g. checkbox(1).checked === true (last row) and/or store.items()[0].watched === true.
